### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained each of A20, A21, A22, A23, A26, A31, A32 and A37 exactly once. In the later window, A20, A21, A23 and A26 still appear in every trace, but A22 appears in only about 54 in 100 traces, and each of A31, A32 and A37 in about 47 in 100. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- A20's successor changed: before, its outgoing transitions went to A31, A32 and A37 in roughly equal thirds; in the later window, about 995 in 1000 go directly to A23, and the distance from A20 to A23 shrank from four event positions to one. [DIR001, LAG001]
- The three activities A31, A32, A37 still run together as a block in no fixed internal order in both windows, but the block moved: before it always preceded A23, A21, A22 and A26; in the later window it follows A23 and A21 (A21 precedes the group in about 46.5 in 100 co-occurrences, versus never before) and still precedes A26. Its mean relative position moved from about 0.40 to about 0.58. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- A22 and the group became mutually exclusive: before, A22 always co-occurred with A31/A32/A37, which preceded it; in the later window they co-occur in about 1 in 200 traces — A22 runs without the group in about 53 in 100 traces, and the group runs without A22 in about 47 in 100. [REL011, REL012, REL013]
- Before, A21 always led to A22; in the later window A21 leads to A22 in about 54 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and to the group in about 46 in 100. Matching this, the A21-to-A26 distance, previously always two positions, is now two positions in about 54 in 100 traces (via A22) and four positions in about 46 in 100 (via the group). [DIR002, REL005, LAG005]
- A23 and A21 now sit earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.45 to 0.39, and 0.60 to 0.54). [POS004, POS002]
- The lag items describing the group's exact spacing in the later window rest on a single observation each and are weak. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment between A20 and A26 was restructured. In the earlier window every case ran A20, then the group A31/A32/A37, then A23, A21, A22 and A26, all mandatory. In the later window, A20 leads directly to A23 and A21, after which the case takes one of two mutually exclusive branches — A22 alone in about 54 in 100 cases, or the group A31/A32/A37 in about 47 in 100 — before A26. The group thereby changed from a mandatory stage before A23 into an alternative to A22 placed after A21. [DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

The reorder and the exclusivity are shown directly by relational, directional and lag evidence rather than inferred from participation alone; the pattern is consistent across the occurrence, direction, position, relation and lag indicators; and 47 items qualified against roughly 0.5 expected for an unchanged process, so chance sampling cannot account for the ensemble. The evidence cannot show whether the branch choice is a routing decision within each case or a mixture of two case populations that behave differently. [DIR001, REL011, REL012, REL013, LAG001, LAG005, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

Other differences: A20's mean relative position moved slightly later (about 0.34 to 0.36) and A26's slightly earlier (about 0.66 to 0.63); these are minor and consistent with being consequences of the same restructuring rather than separate changes. [POS001, POS005]
